first_impression.reaction: Okay, the first paragraph actually answers what I typed. Getting ready late morning, photos before or after, drinks, dinner in the evening, and check sunset. Good. But I still don't have a single actual clock time until I scroll past the takeaways and a fluffy 'four movements' bit. On the train I want '3.30pm guests, 6pm reception' up top.

journey.quote: A wedding timeline for a 4pm ceremony puts getting ready in the late morning, photos either before the ceremony (with a first look) or straight after it, drinks as the light softens, and dinner and speeches into the evening.
journey.reaction: Direct answer in the first sentence. This is why I stay.

journey.quote: A first look moves the couple and wedding party photos before 4pm, so you join your guests for drinks.
journey.reaction: Useful, but none of the takeaways has a single time in it. I came for a timeline. Give me the key times right here and I could screenshot it and leave.

journey.section: The 4pm wedding timeline at a glance
journey.quote: Think of a 4pm day in four movements. The morning belongs to getting ready.
journey.reaction: The heading says 'at a glance' but it's poetry, not a glance. No times. This is the bit I'd skim past.

journey.section: A 4pm wedding timeline with a first look
journey.quote: **3.30pm.** The couple goes out of sight. Guests arrive and are seated.
journey.reaction: This is exactly what I wanted. Bold times, one line each, easy on a phone. This is the section I'd screenshot.

journey.section: A 4pm wedding timeline with a first look
journey.quote: Every clock time on this page is a planning example to adapt, not a rule.
journey.reaction: Fair and honest. Doesn't pretend there's one right answer.

journey.section: How sunset shapes a 4pm wedding day
journey.quote: If it falls before 4.30pm, the ceremony is your golden light and portraits belong before it, which makes a first look worth a serious thought.
journey.reaction: Didn't think of that. That's actually a useful tip and makes me trust the page more than the usual listicles.

journey.section: How sunset shapes a 4pm wedding day
journey.quote: By the end of evening civil twilight, when the centre of the sun is 6 degrees below the horizon, large objects can be seen but no detail can be made out without artificial light.
journey.reaction: Bit too science class for me on a train. I get the point (turn the lights on early) but I'd skip this paragraph.

journey.quote: For example, put 3.30pm on the invitation as the arrival time and 4pm as the start, so guests can find a seat and settle.
journey.reaction: Good FAQ. Short, direct, real question I'd actually Google next.

journey.section: Planning a 4pm ceremony at a destination wedding
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, works in your time zone, and is your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: Not why I'm here. I don't know who these people are. It's not pushy though, and it's not a pop-up, so I don't mind.

unanswered_questions: Who wrote this, and when was it last updated? I can't tell if it's current.
Is there a printable or downloadable version of the timeline, or do I have to copy the table myself?

turn_offs_found.quote: Think of a 4pm day in four movements. The morning belongs to getting ready. The early afternoon belongs to photos, if you choose a first look. The ceremony and drinks carry you from 4pm into the soft light, and the reception takes the evening through to the send-off.
turn_offs_found.why: Heading promises 'at a glance' and I get flowery prose with no times. Feels like fluff between me and the answer.

would_share_with: My fiancé, as a screenshot of the first-look timeline
My sister, who keeps asking what time the reception would start

cta_reaction.quote: If you would rather hand the venue questions to one person, Wedded Concierge pairs you with a Wedded Advisor for the whole plan.
cta_reaction.why: I came for a timeline and I'm not planning a destination wedding with a planner right now. The links don't annoy me, they're just not for me. I might bookmark the page though.
